questions.question: Explain, using a parallel line, why the interior angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees.
questions.expected_answer: Draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The two angles it makes with the triangle's sides are alternate to the two angles at the other vertices and so equal them. Together with the angle at the vertex they lie along a straight line and add to 180, so the three interior angles add to 180.

questions.question: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40 degrees. Find the base angles with reasons.
questions.expected_answer: The base angles are equal, base angles of an isosceles triangle, and the three angles add to 180, angle sum of a triangle. So the two base angles together are 180 minus 40, which is 140, and each is 70 degrees.

questions.question: A triangle has angles x, 2x and 3x. Find x, the angles and the triangle's classification.
questions.expected_answer: The sum 6x equals 180, so x is 30 and the angles are 30, 60 and 90. The triangle is right-angled, and since all angles differ, its sides differ too, so it is scalene: a scalene right-angled triangle.
